lateFindings.what: One surface was not behind a wrapper, and the test pass found it after CP1 was filed. CP1 listed lib/r1BriefCompose.ts as a consumer 'covered by the change with no per-surface wiring'; that is wrong for its FLOOD section, which consumes parcelRecordFactRead.loadParcelRecordFloodFact (the P-152 Consumer-C read) DIRECTLY and UNGATED -- unlike the zoning and setbacks wrappers, whose facts only ever exist for a slated pair.
lateFindings.consequence: Making every non-value flood state a refusal unconditionally (which the first cut of this card did) refuses flood for UNSLATED counties too, where the pre-cutover atoms path is still the answer; P-297 forbids that ('unslated rails keep their current path'). Two pre-existing tests in src/__tests__/pe-r1-brief-flood.test.ts caught it by failing, which is why the fix is in this commit rather than in a follow-up.
lateFindings.fix: composeFloodBriefSection asks isSlatedForCellServe -- the same one-rule function every wrapper asks -- off the fact's own place_key (the store's `<fips>:<prop_id>` grammar). Slated pair: value/absent-verified as before, not-applicable is the stated absence, refused/unaccounted is a declared refusal with the cell's reason and the atom is not consulted. Unslated pair, or a read that could not place itself (place_key null, an unparseable node id): unchanged fall-through.
